claims.title: Inference requests may be intercepted between calling services and the gateway
claims.description: `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:serving-edge` and carries end-user text tagged `pii`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport encryption is not enforced, an attacker able to observe this internet-facing path reads submitted inference requests in transit. The disclosed prompts can reveal end-user personal information and provide content useful for targeted attacks against the calling teams.

quotes.text:
Other teams' backends call our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE
that we expose on the internet because two of the calling services are in a
different cloud.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high and conditional on the unknown transport-encryption state because the flow crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway`, making the observer population broad. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and carries end-user text, but the model does not establish corpus-scale capture.

mitigations.detail: Set and verify TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request`, including certificate validation by calling services.
Avoid sending unnecessary personal data in inference requests and use opaque references where the gateway can resolve data server-side.

claims.title: Gateway-to-model-server requests may be readable across the serving boundary
claims.description: `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network`, carries a `pii` inference-request payload, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If this internal hop is unencrypted, an attacker with visibility on the boundary path can intercept customer prompts. Those prompts may expose the same user-supplied data retained in `store:inference-log` and can aid later targeting of the affected calling teams.

quotes.text:
The gateway forwards the request to the model server, which runs the actual
model on GPU nodes in our model network.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown encryption state: the attacker must gain observation capability on the serving-edge-to-model-network path, but the path is a stated boundary crossing. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii` inference requests and prompt disclosure is irreversible once captured.

mitigations.detail: Require mTLS between `process:inference-gateway` and `process:model-server` and record the verified `encryption_in_transit` posture on the flow.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be intercepted while the model server loads them
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` transfers model artifacts from `store:model-registry-bucket` to `process:model-server` with `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the object-storage connection is not protected, a network observer can read proprietary model artifacts during startup. The disclosed artifact can enable model extraction, offline analysis, and more targeted attacks on the inference service.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown encryption state because an attacker must first obtain a position on the internal model-network path and observe a startup load. Impact is medium because the transferred model artifact is tagged `business-critical-data` and disclosure can enable offline analysis of the service model.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated TLS for registry access
mitigations.detail: Configure and verify TLS for `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact`, with the model-server workload identity validating the registry endpoint.

claims.title: Customer features may be intercepted on the model-server-to-Redis read path
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` carries per-customer account age and spend bands tagged `pii` and `financial`, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If Redis traffic is unencrypted, an attacker able to observe the model-network path can intercept customer feature records. The records enable customer profiling and can be correlated with inference activity handled by `process:model-server`.

quotes.text:
The features include account age and
spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown transport-encryption state because an attacker needs an internal model-network observation point. Impact is high because the flow carries customer-specific `pii` and `financial` data from confidential `store:redis-feature-store`, potentially across the feature corpus.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` and authenticate the Redis endpoint to the model server.

mitigations.summary: Reduce feature exposure on the wire
mitigations.detail: Return only the feature fields required for a given inference request and avoid transmitting raw customer identifiers where opaque lookups are possible.

claims.title: Raw prompts and responses may be intercepted while written to the inference log
claims.description: `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log` sends raw prompts and model responses from the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway` to `store:inference-log`, with `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If that logging hop lacks transport encryption, an observer on the path can intercept debugging records containing end-user text. Captured records create a second copy of sensitive prompt content outside the request path and can support profiling of calling-team users.

quotes.text:
The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in
BigQuery, for debugging. That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever
the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown encryption state because the source is an internet-facing gateway and the attacker needs path visibility to the logging connection. Impact is medium because the log contains raw prompts that may carry user-provided personal content, though the model does not establish a specific volume or classification beyond `pii`.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with endpoint validation on `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log`.

mitigations.summary: Redact prompt logging at the gateway
mitigations.detail: Log correlation IDs and approved diagnostic fields by default; redact or tokenize raw prompts and model responses before they reach `store:inference-log`.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be intercepted while engineers publish them
claims.description: `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact` transfers model artifacts to `store:model-registry-bucket` with `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the publishing connection is not encrypted, an attacker observing that path can read model artifacts in transit. The copied artifact can be analyzed offline and may reveal business-critical model behavior before it is deployed to `process:model-server`.

quotes.text: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown encryption state because an attacker must observe the engineer-to-registry path in the model network. Impact is medium because model artifacts are tagged `business-critical-data` and disclosure enables offline study of the deployed model.

mitigations.detail: Use authenticated TLS for `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact` and verify the storage endpoint before artifact upload.

claims.title: Registry artifacts are exposed by storage-layer copies if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:model-registry-bucket` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown` and holds business-critical model artifacts. If that unknown resolves to no encryption at rest, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy, such as an operational snapshot or exported object copy, can read the artifacts without using the model server's normal service-account path. The copied model can then be analyzed offline to reveal business-critical behavior and improve attacks against inference operations.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest-encryption state: obtaining a storage-layer copy requires access to storage operations, but does not require compromising the application read path. Impact is medium because the bucket contains `business-critical-data` model artifacts whose disclosure enables offline analysis.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for registry objects and copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest posture for `store:model-registry-bucket`, then require KMS-managed encryption for objects, backups, snapshots, and exports, with export permissions restricted to dedicated principals.

claims.title: Confidential Redis features are exposed by storage-layer copies if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:redis-feature-store` is classified confidential, contains `pii` and `financial` customer features, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If storage encryption is absent, an attacker obtaining a volume, snapshot, backup, or other storage-layer copy can read account-age and spend-band records without authenticating through `process:model-server`. This can expose the feature corpus for customer profiling and can be correlated with other customer data obtained elsewhere.

quotes.text:
The features include account age and
spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown encryption-at-rest state because storage-layer access or copied media is required but bypasses the live Redis read path. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and holds customer-specific `pii` and `financial` features, making corpus disclosure harmful and irreversible.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt Redis data and operational copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:redis-feature-store` encryption at rest, require managed keys for persistence, backups, and snapshots, and limit who may create or restore copies.

mitigations.summary: Separate access to data and encryption keys
mitigations.detail: Restrict key-use permissions independently from Redis administration and storage-export permissions.

claims.title: Raw prompt logs are exposed by storage-layer copies if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:inference-log` retains every request and response, including raw prompts, and its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the BigQuery-backed log storage or its operational copies are unencrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy can read retained user text without going through `process:inference-gateway`. This turns transient request content into a durable disclosure source that can reveal personal or sensitive information supplied by calling-team users.

quotes.text:
The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in
BigQuery, for debugging. That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever
the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown encryption-at-rest state because storage-layer access is required but bypasses application authentication. Impact is medium because `store:inference-log` is tagged `pii` and retains raw user prompts, although its classification and the sensitivity of every prompt are unknown.

mitigations.summary: Verify at-rest protection for the inference log
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for `store:inference-log`, including exports, backups, and retained operational copies.
Stop storing full raw prompts and responses by default, redact sensitive fields at `process:inference-gateway`, and apply a short retention policy to necessary diagnostic records.

claims.title: An internal foothold may permit direct reading of Redis customer features
claims.description: `store:redis-feature-store` contains confidential customer account-age and spend-band data. The source states that Redis has no password, while `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` leaves its authentication state unresolved. An attacker who gains a foothold in `boundary:model-network` may be able to connect directly and read feature records if no other Redis authentication or authorization mechanism is enforced. The disclosed `pii` and `financial` features enable customer profiling independently of the model server's normal request handling.

quotes.text:
Redis has no password on it; it is
only reachable inside the model network.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker needs an internal model-network foothold, but the source states Redis has no password and the flow authentication is unresolved. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and contains customer-specific `pii` and `financial` data that can be read in bulk.

mitigations.summary: Require Redis authentication and least-privilege authorization
mitigations.detail: Configure a dedicated authenticated Redis principal for `process:model-server`, deny anonymous reads, and restrict that principal to only the required feature keys.
Enforce network policy so only `process:model-server` can reach the Redis service port, while treating that restriction as defense in depth rather than the sole access control.

claims.title: A compromised model server can read registry artifacts using its workload identity
claims.description: `process:model-server` reads `store:model-registry-bucket` using its own service account. If an attacker compromises the model server, they inherit that workload identity and can read the model artifact through `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact`. The artifact can be copied for offline analysis, exposing business-critical model behavior; this remains conditional on the model server compromise and on the service account's effective read scope, which the model does not state.

quotes.text: It uses its own service account for that.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because exploiting this path first requires compromise of `process:model-server`, whose exposure is unknown and which is placed in the model network. Impact is medium because the inherited identity can read model artifacts tagged `business-critical-data`, enabling offline analysis once copied.

mitigations.summary: Scope the model-server workload identity narrowly
mitigations.detail: Grant the model-server service account read-only access only to the specific approved artifact versions it must load, with no bucket listing, export, or unrelated object permissions.

mitigations.summary: Protect artifact access after workload compromise
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived workload credentials, restrict object-download paths to the model server, and alert on artifact reads inconsistent with startup behavior.
